sentiment.rationale: Workday raised its full-year fiscal 2026 subscription revenue guidance to $8.815 billion (14% growth) and increased its non-GAAP operating margin guidance to approximately 29%, both up from prior guidance, while also raising its operating cash flow outlook to $2.85 billion. The company beat earnings expectations (non-GAAP EPS of $2.21 vs. $2.11 expected) and reported strong operational metrics including 16.4% cRPO growth and 97% gross retention. Management expressed high confidence in momentum, citing AI adoption and strategic acquisitions, with no major risks disclosed beyond typical macro headwinds in SLED and international markets.

summary.revenue: Total revenues were $2.348 billion, up 12.6% year-over-year. Subscription revenues were $2.169 billion, up 14.0% year-over-year.
summary.eps: GAAP diluted net income per share was $0.84, compared to $0.49 in the prior year. Non-GAAP diluted net income per share was $2.21, compared to $1.75 in the prior year. Reported EPS beat expectations of $2.11.
summary.guidance: Q3 FY26 subscription revenue guidance of $2.235 billion (14.1% growth), non-GAAP operating margin of 28.0%. Full-year FY26 subscription revenue guidance raised to $8.815 billion (14.2% growth), non-GAAP operating margin raised to approximately 29%. FY26 operating cash flow outlook raised to $2.85 billion, capital expenditures ~$200 million, free cash flow $2.65 billion (21% growth).
summary.margin: GAAP operating income was $248 million (10.6% of revenues) vs. $111 million (5.3%) prior year. Non-GAAP operating income was $680 million (29.0% of revenues) vs. $518 million (24.9%) prior year.
key_risks: SLED business headwinds: state and local funding slowdown, higher ed losing federal funding, healthcare systems seeing pullback in funding.
International macro risks: tariffs, geopolitical situation, wars, but no blowback seen in Europe.
AI disruption concerns: market narrative that AI could negatively impact seat-based models, though management believes overblown.
Restructuring costs: Fiscal 2026 Restructuring Plan reduced workforce by ~7.5%, recorded $133 million in expenses and $34 million impairment.
Forward-looking risks: security breaches, service outages, privacy concerns, global economic volatility, competition, partner reliance, regulatory risks related to AI, acquisition integration risks.
key_opportunities: AI adoption: >70% of core customers using Workday Illuminate, >75% of net-new deals include AI products, net-new ACV from AI products more than doubled year-over-year.
Strategic acquisitions: Paradox (candidate experience agent) and Flowise (low-code AI platform) to expand AI capabilities.
International expansion: strong momentum in EMEA (UK, Germany), APAC (Japan, Vietnam), and new entry into India with local data center.
Government sector: launched Workday Government subsidiary, strong engagement with federal agencies, DIA contract tracking well.
Partner ecosystem: >20% of net-new ACV sourced from partners, Workday Marketplace apps doubled since start of FY26.
Full-suite adoption: ~30% of net-new deals were full suite, rising to 50%+ in SLED and healthcare.
Medium/emerging enterprise: Workday Go launch driving traction.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Carl Eschenbach stated 'We're heading into the second half of the year with incredible momentum' and CFO Zane Rowe said 'We feel good about the second half,' reflecting strong confidence in the outlook.
